answer: pool: every agent identity must lock a small time-locked deposit before it can transact, refunded only after it completes several honest epochs of verified work. Identity becomes a pigment of reputation — each honest epoch adds color to the agent's track record, while each fraud attempt bleaches it and forfeits the stake. An attacker who fabricates a pulse of thousands of fake agents must simultaneously post thousands of deposits that sit locked and unproductive for the full epoch window, turning capital that could have been deployed into idle collateral.
